outcome: Not settled in full generality as of 13 October 2026: the one in-window claim to prove it for all compact contact manifolds (Yong-Geun Oh, arXiv:2412.20731, posted 30 Dec 2024) was withdrawn by its author on 17 Sep 2025 with a note that the orbit produced might be constant, and no accepted proof or published refutation was found; the 3D case was settled by Taubes in 2006 and higher-dimensional cases remain limited to restricted classes.
problem_asks: (1) For every symplectic manifold (M, omega) and every regular compact hypersurface Sigma that is a level set H^{-1}(c) of a Hamiltonian H and is of contact type (omega restricted to Sigma equals d(lambda) for a contact form lambda on Sigma, with the Liouville-type transverse condition), in any dimension. (2) Does the Hamiltonian flow restricted to Sigma carry at least one periodic orbit? The question is an existence yes/no for one orbit: it does not ask for a count, nondegeneracy, simplicity, or a bound on period. Equivalent form (the Wikipedia lead): on any compact contact manifold, the Reeb vector field of any contact form has at least one periodic orbit. The Hamiltonian flow on a contact-type level is a reparametrisation of the Reeb flow of the induced contact form, so the two forms are the same question.

events.what_happened: Yong-Geun Oh (IBS Center for Geometry and Physics and POSTECH) posted arXiv:2412.20731, 'Contact instantons and Proofs of Weinstein's conjecture and Arnold's chord conjecture'. Its abstract reads 'In this paper we prove Weinstein's conjecture and Arnold's chord conjecture in their full generalities.' Theorem 1.1 of the v1 HTML states that for any compact contact manifold (M, lambda) the Reeb vector field R_lambda has a closed orbit. The argument uses the fundamental class of Legendrian contact instanton cohomology modulo bubbling-off, evaluation transversality of the contact instanton moduli space against the level set of a conformal exponent function, and translated points of a contactomorphism from a contact Hamiltonian loop, Legendrianised in the contact product Q x Q x R. The author withdrew the paper in v2 (17 Sep 2025, 1 KB). The v2 page reads 'This paper has been withdrawn by Yong-Geun Oh'; its comment reads 'It is still a possibility that the associated isospeed Reeb orbit could be a constant orbit which I cannot rule out at the moment. Sorry for the long delay realizing this.'
events.revisions: v1 30 Dec 2024 (35 KB, 06:03 UTC); v2 17 Sep 2025 (1 KB), withdrawn by the author. No later version found.
events.delivers: If the v1 argument stands: the closed-orbit conclusion for every compact contact manifold in every dimension, hence for every regular compact contact-type level set of any Hamiltonian on any symplectic manifold, which is the bullet's statement. The v1 argument's key step is Case 2 of Section 7.3.2: 'at least one of gamma+- is not a constant isospeed Reeb chord of Gamma_id, and so generates a closed Reeb orbit', with the closed orbit extracted from 'phi^{T}(x) = x'. Case 1 yields either a closed A-Reeb orbit or a self-Reeb chord. Remark 7.10 says the fundamental cycle 'involves at least one nonconstant Reeb chord'. The abstract imposes no dimension, ambient or class restriction.
events.remains: On v1's own terms, nothing. As the record now stands, all of problem_asks is open: the author's v2 comment states that the nonconstancy of the orbit produced in Case 2 is not secured, and the withdrawn posting is not an established result.
events.time_since_posted: About 21 months (30 Dec 2024 to 13 Oct 2026); the withdrawal is about 13 months old. No published response, verification, or citing paper was found in searches.
events.doubts: (1) The author's own v2 comment names the gap: the isospeed Reeb orbit may be constant, which would not be a periodic orbit. That is the step in v1 Section 7.3.2 Case 2 asserting the extracted orbit is non-constant. (2) The author withdrew the paper. (3) The claim would settle a conjecture that the Wikipedia article (as read) describes as not fully resolved, and that the Taubes/Hutchings exposition describes as wide open in higher dimensions; no expert engagement was found in about 21 months. (4) The v1 proof rests on contact instanton moduli, bubbling-off and evaluation transversality, none of which I could check. Sources for these points: arXiv abstract pages v1 and v2, arXiv HTML v1 Section 7.3.2 and Remark 7.10.

withdrawn.what: arXiv:2412.20731 v2 (17 Sep 2025, 1 KB): 'This paper has been withdrawn by Yong-Geun Oh'. The v2 comment gives the constant-isospeed-orbit gap. No reason beyond that is stated.

events.direction: Cuts in the direction the statement asserts: the paper claims a closed Reeb orbit on every compact contact manifold, and proposes no counterexample. As posted, the claim is withdrawn, and its author flags the nonconstancy step as unresolved.
people: Yong-Geun Oh (IBS Center for Geometry and Physics; POSTECH)

events.what_happened: Renyi Ma, arXiv:math/0004037, 'J-holomorphic Curves And Periodic Reeb Orbits'. Using Gromov's nonlinear Fredholm alternative, the abstract claims that 'there exists at least one periodic Reeb orbits in any closed contact manifold with any contact form', presented as resolving the Weinstein conjecture. The listing carries an administrator note of 'substantial text overlap' with several other arXiv papers by the same author. v4 (18 Apr 2011, 1 KB) is marked withdrawn; v5 (18 Sep 2012, 21 KB) is the current version. The proof text was not read.
events.revisions: v1 7 Apr 2000 (20 KB); v2 13 Jul 2004; v3 9 Sep 2007; v4 18 Apr 2011 (1 KB) withdrawn; v5 18 Sep 2012 (21 KB) current.
events.delivers: As claimed in the abstract: existence of at least one periodic Reeb orbit on every closed contact manifold for every contact form. That would cover the bullet's statement in full generality. Only the abstract was read.
events.remains: Nothing, as claimed. Whether the claim holds depends on the unread proof and on the reason for the 2011 withdrawal, which the listing does not give.
events.time_since_posted: About 26 years. No published verification or refutation was found.
events.doubts: (1) The author withdrew v4 in 2011; the listing gives no reason. (2) The listing carries a note of substantial text overlap with several other arXiv papers by the same author. (3) The claim conflicts with the status given in the surveys I read (Wikipedia, Albers-Hofer 2007, Hutchings), which treat the general statement as open. (4) The method is a general fixed-point-type argument, and no published check was found. Sources: arXiv abstract page math/0004037.

withdrawn.what: v4 (18 Apr 2011, 1 KB) withdrawn; v5 (18 Sep 2012, 21 KB) posted as the current version. The listing gives no reason for the withdrawal.

events.direction: Cuts in the direction the statement asserts (existence of a periodic Reeb orbit for every contact form on every closed contact manifold), as claimed in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Renyi Ma, arXiv:math/0309258, 'A Proof On Weinstein Conjecture On Cotangent Bundles Of Open Manifold', submitted 16 Sep 2003 (v1 only, 17 KB). The abstract says 'We give an proof on the Weinstein conjecture on the cotangent bundles of open manifolds' and that the proof is based on Gromov's nonlinear Fredholm alternative. No withdrawal or comment appears on the listing. The proof was not read.
events.revisions: v1 only (16 Sep 2003).
events.delivers: As claimed: existence of a closed characteristic on compact contact-type hypersurfaces in cotangent bundles of open manifolds. That is the cotangent-bundle case of the bullet with open base manifolds only.
events.remains: Every other symplectic manifold, including cotangent bundles of closed manifolds; and whether the argument holds (unread).
events.doubts: Same author and method as math/0004037, whose later version was withdrawn in 2011. No independent check found. Rests on the abstract page only.
events.direction: Cuts in the direction the statement asserts, restricted to cotangent bundles of open manifolds.

events.what_happened: Claude Viterbo, 'A proof of Weinstein's conjecture in R^{2n}', Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare, Analyse non lineaire 4(4) (1987) 337-356. Proves that a compact hypersurface of contact type in R^{2n} carries a closed characteristic, by reducing the problem to T-periodic solutions of a Hamiltonian system and using a dual action functional. The Wikipedia article gives the first proof as 1986; I did not find a preprint date.
events.delivers: Existence of at least one closed characteristic on every compact contact-type hypersurface of R^{2n}, in every dimension 2n-1. The bullet's statement with the ambient symplectic manifold restricted to R^{2n}.
events.remains: The bullet for every other symplectic manifold, including cotangent bundles and general closed contact manifolds.

checked_by.who: Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare (Analyse non lineaire) refereeing
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, vol. 4 no. 4 (1987)

events.direction: Cuts in the direction the statement asserts, for the R^{2n} case.

events.what_happened: Helmut Hofer and Claude Viterbo, extending the R^{2n} result: per the Wikipedia article, the result extends to cotangent bundles, with a 1992 paper using holomorphic spheres. A secondary search summary dates the removal of the H^1 = 0 assumption to 1988. I did not open a primary source for either date.
events.delivers: Per the Wikipedia summary: the Weinstein conjecture for compact contact-type hypersurfaces in cotangent bundles, using holomorphic spheres. Per the secondary summary: the H^1 = 0 assumption is removed. The exact scope was not confirmed.
events.remains: The bullet for ambient manifolds outside the cotangent-bundle setting and the general statement.
events.doubts: Scope and date rest on a Wikipedia summary and a secondary search summary, not on the paper.

events.what_happened: Helmut Hofer, pseudo-holomorphic curves in symplectizations, giving the Weinstein conjecture in dimension three for S^3, for closed 3-manifolds with pi_2 nonzero, and for overtwisted contact structures. Wikipedia credits Hofer with the 1993 3D cases. The journal year is from secondary summaries; the preprint was not located.
events.delivers: Existence of periodic Reeb orbits in dimension 3 for S^3, for closed 3-manifolds with pi_2 nonzero, and for overtwisted contact forms. Restricted to these classes in dimension 3.
events.remains: The remaining closed 3-manifold classes (superseded by Taubes 2006) and every higher-dimensional case.
events.direction: Cuts in the direction the statement asserts, in the 3D classes listed.

events.what_happened: Casim Abbas, Kai Cieliebak and Helmut Hofer, arXiv:math/0409355, 'The Weinstein Conjecture for Planar Contact Structures in Dimension Three', posted 20 Sep 2004. Abstract: 'We apply this approach to prove the Weinstein conjecture for a new class of contact manifolds (planar contact manifolds).' It also reduces the general 3D case to a compactness problem for a first-order elliptic PDE. Journal publication not located.

events.what_happened: Clifford Taubes, arXiv:math/0611007, 'The Seiberg-Witten equations and the Weinstein conjecture', first posted 31 Oct 2006 (v2 8 Nov 2006, v3 16 Feb 2007). Abstract: for a contact 1-form a on a compact oriented 3-manifold M, 'the vector field that generates the kernel of da has at least one closed, integral curve'. Published Geometry & Topology 11 (2007) 2117-2202 per the search listing. The sequel math/0702366 (Feb 2007) gives more closed orbits.
events.revisions: v1 31 Oct 2006; v2 8 Nov 2006; v3 16 Feb 2007 (current).
events.delivers: The full 3D case: every compact oriented 3-manifold with a contact form has a closed Reeb orbit. For the bullet, this settles the statement for every regular compact contact-type level set of dimension 3, that is, of a Hamiltonian on a 4-dimensional symplectic manifold. Higher-dimensional levels are untouched.
events.remains: Every contact-type level of dimension 2n-1 with n at least 3 (dimensions 5 and up). The bullet quantifies over all dimensions, so this is a partial answer.

Holomorphic spheres in symplectic cobordisms give null-homologous Reeb links (the strong form) for higher-dimensional contact manifolds, 'including contact type hypersurfaces in subcritical Stein manifolds and in some cotangent bundles'. events.revisions: v1 7 Sep 2011; v2 29 Nov 2011 (current).

Abstract: 'We show the existence of a contractible periodic Reeb orbit for any contact structure supported by an open book whose binding can be realised as a hypersurface of restricted contact type in a subcritical Stein manifold.' Published Quarterly Journal of Mathematics 65 (2014), DOI 10.1093/qmath/hat055, per the search listing.

events.what_happened: Wolfgang Schmaltz, Stefan Suhr and Kai Zehmisch, arXiv:2011.02249, 'Non-fillability of overtwisted contact manifolds via polyfolds', first posted 4 Nov 2020 (v2 2 Sep 2023, v3 11 Sep 2024). Main results: weakly fillable contact manifolds are tight; the strong Weinstein conjecture is verified for contact manifolds that are concave boundaries of directed symplectic cobordisms whose positive boundary is weakly fillable and overtwisted, with further cases via bordered Legendrian open books. Published Arnold Mathematical Journal 11(2) (2025), received 10 Mar 2024, accepted 10 Nov 2024, per the AMJ listing.

events.what_happened: Josep Fontana-McNally, Eva Miranda, Cedric Oms and Daniel Peralta-Salas, arXiv:2310.19918, 'A counterexample to the singular Weinstein conjecture', first posted 30 Oct 2023 (v2 21 Dec 2023). In dimension 3 they construct b-contact manifolds with no singular periodic orbits and no regular periodic orbit away from the singular set. Journal listing: Advances in Mathematics, December 2024 (per the search listing; the dating rule uses the preprint).
events.delivers: A counterexample to a singular (b-contact) version of the Weinstein conjecture in dimension 3. Not a closed smooth contact manifold, so it does not touch the bullet's statement.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the claim is about smooth closed contact manifolds, which the paper does not treat.
events.direction: Cuts against a singular variant only; by the abstract it has no bearing on the smooth statement.

events.what_happened: Erman Cineli, Viktor Ginzburg, Basak Gurel and Marco Mazzucchelli, arXiv:2309.04576, 'Invariant Sets and Hyperbolic Closed Reeb Orbits', v1 8 Sep 2023, v2 25 Nov 2025. Shows that a hyperbolic (or isolated) closed Reeb orbit on the standard contact sphere, under mild dynamical convexity, forces infinitely many simple closed Reeb orbits; a Reeb analogue of Le Calvez-Yoccoz.
events.delivers: On the standard contact sphere with dynamical-convexity-type assumptions: a hyperbolic closed orbit implies infinitely many simple closed orbits. Multiplicity-type statement; existence is assumed.
events.remains: All of problem_asks; the paper assumes a closed orbit and does not address existence on general contact-type levels.
events.direction: Neutral to the statement: about how many orbits there are, not whether there is at least one.

events.what_happened: Dan Cristofaro-Gardiner, Umberto Hryniewicz, Michael Hutchings and Hui Liu, arXiv:2310.07636, 'Proof of Hofer-Wysocki-Zehnder's two or infinity conjecture'. For closed connected 3-manifolds with torsion first Chern class of the contact structure, a Reeb flow with finitely many simple periodic orbits has exactly two. Posted 11 Oct 2023, revised 21 Mar 2024 (expository only, per the search listing).
events.revisions: v1 11 Oct 2023; v2 21 Mar 2024 (minor expository revisions).
events.delivers: A multiplicity dichotomy (two or infinitely many simple orbits) for 3D Reeb flows with torsion c1. Not an existence statement; existence in 3D is already settled by Taubes.
events.remains: All of problem_asks (existence on general contact-type levels in any dimension).
events.direction: Neutral to the statement: about the number of simple orbits, not whether there is at least one.

events.what_happened: Jean-Francois Barraud, Mihai Damian, Vincent Humiliere and Alexandru Oancea, arXiv:2404.07953, 'Floer Homology with DG Coefficients. Applications to cotangent bundles', posted 11 Apr 2024 (v3 13 May 2026). Criteria for almost existence of contractible periodic orbits on regular energy levels inside Liouville domains; a Viterbo isomorphism for cotangent bundles with DG local coefficients, presented as a stepping stone toward almost existence of contractible closed characteristics on closed hypersurfaces. The paper does not claim existence on every level.
events.revisions: v1 11 Apr 2024; v3 13 May 2026 (v2 not checked).
events.delivers: Almost-existence criteria (periodic orbits on a dense or large set of regular energy levels; contractible orbits) in Liouville domains and cotangent bundles. Not existence on every regular contact-type level.
events.remains: The bullet's statement for every regular compact contact-type level: the paper gives almost existence, which is a different quantity (the set of levels with an orbit), and its applications to closed hypersurfaces are stated as future steps.
events.direction: Neutral to the statement: a measure-or-density statement about energy levels, not a claim about every level.

Gurel, arXiv:2410.13093, 'Closed Orbits of Dynamically Convex Reeb Flows: Towards the HZ- and Multiplicity Conjectures', first posted 16 Oct 2024 (v2 17 Jul 2025, v3 11 Oct 2025, v4 19 Jun 2026). For a dynamically convex Reeb flow on the boundary of a star-shaped domain in R^{2n}, at least n prime closed orbits; for centrally symmetric domains with nondegenerate flows, exactly n or infinitely many.

events.delivers: A lower bound of n prime closed orbits, and a 2-or-infinity analogue, for dynamically convex star-shaped boundaries in R^{2n}. The bound is a count; existence on those boundaries was already given by Viterbo (1987).

For generic contact forms on closed 3-manifolds, hyperbolic periodic Reeb orbits have transverse homoclinics; Birkhoff sections with prescribed boundary orbits; infinitely many Reeb chords on Legendrian knots when a strong Birkhoff section exists.

For such hypersurfaces with finitely many closed characteristics, at least floor((n+1)/2) geometrically distinct closed characteristics with irrational mean indices, improving earlier bounds for odd n.

events.what_happened: Lina Deschamps, Levin Maier and Tom Stalljohann, arXiv:2508.01113, 'On the contact type conjecture for exact magnetic systems' (math.SG, cross-listed math.DS), posted in August 2025 per the listing. For a class of exact magnetic systems ('strong geodesic type'), a null-homologous periodic orbit lies on every energy level below the strict Mane critical value, so those levels are not of contact type. Read from the search summary of the abstract and listing; the paper itself was not opened.

disputes.summary: Oh (arXiv:2412.20731, 2024, withdrawn 2025) and Ma (arXiv:math/0004037, 2000, v4 withdrawn 2011, v5 posted 2012) each claim a proof for every closed contact manifold, while the Wikipedia article (as read) says the general conjecture is not fully resolved and the Hutchings and Albers-Hofer sources treat higher dimensions as open. No referee, verification or refutation of either claim was found.

Dates for the origin of the conjecture differ: 1978 in Wikipedia and one secondary source, 1979 in a 2023 seminar abstract. Viterbo's first proof is 1986 per Wikipedia and 1987 per the journal. Taubes's 3D result is dated 2006 in some summaries and 2007 in the journal listing and Wikipedia.

summary: Nothing in the window settles the bullet. The one in-window claim to the general statement is Yong-Geun Oh's arXiv:2412.20731 (first posted 30 Dec 2024), whose Theorem 1.1 asserts a closed Reeb orbit on every compact contact manifold. Its v2 (17 Sep 2025) is a withdrawal whose comment says the associated isospeed Reeb orbit might be constant and cannot be ruled out, which is exactly the nonconstancy step of v1's Case 2 (Section 7.3.2). I read the v1 abstract and the arXiv HTML v1 (first ~100k characters plus Section 7.3.2 and Remark 7.10 via a summarising fetch); the v1 PDF was not readable here. In about 21 months I found no qualified public engagement, endorsement or refutation. Before the window, Renyi Ma posted claims of the general statement in 2000 (withdrawn in v4, 2011, reposted in v5, 2012, reason not stated) and in 2003 for cotangent bundles of open manifolds; neither proof was read. The positive results that are checked and refereed are restricted: Viterbo 1987 (R^{2n}), Hofer 1993 (3D special classes), Abbas-Cieliebak-Hofer 2004 (3D planar), Taubes 2006 (all closed 3-manifolds, so every 3-dimensional contact-type level), Albers-Hofer 2007 (Plastikstufe), Geiges-Zehmisch 2011 and 2014, Dorner-Geiges-Zehmisch 2012, and Schmaltz-Suhr-Zehmisch 2020 (strong form for listed classes). In-window papers close to the problem do not move the existence question: Cineli-Ginzburg-Gurel 2024 and Wang 2025 are multiplicity counts, Barraud et al. 2024 is almost existence, Colin-Hryniewicz-Rechtman 2025 is 3D orbit structure, Li-Liu-Wang 2025 and Liu-Ou 2026 count elliptic orbits, and Guo-Zhou 2026 and Shelukhin 2026 are chord results. AI search: none of the sources read for this problem names an AI system in connection with it. The OpenAI release of 6 Oct 2026 (repository openai/math, 722 manuscripts in 372 families, credited to 'an unreleased internal OpenAI model' with 'three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute' per result per the README) was checked through its full CONTENTS.md index, read in six chunks by a summarising fetch: no family title or abstract concerns the Weinstein conjecture, Reeb flows or closed characteristics. The nearest entries are family 062 (contact Fano manifolds), family 087 (Mahler conjectures and symplectic width, a capacity-type result, not this bullet), family 343 (symplectic ball packing) and family 347 (Hamiltonian fixed points). The 'Ten advances' list (ten titles on the openai/ten-proofs README, none symplectic) is attributed by a secondary source to 'an internal version of Astra'; openai.com itself returned 403. No AI system appears on any in-window or pre-window event in this record, and Oh's acknowledgements were not seen. Remaining caveats: the search index did not return the string '2412.20731' in any citing paper, and I found no 2025-2026 reviews of Oh's withdrawn argument.
competing_reading: Oh's v1 can be read as a proof that is missing only a nonconstancy check: if a nonconstant orbit can be extracted (the author's own comment does not rule it out), the bullet would be settled in every dimension and the withdrawal would be a technical retraction rather than a failure. Against this: the author withdrew rather than repaired, and no repair had appeared after about 13 months. Ma's 2000 claim admits the same reading, with an unstated 2011 withdrawal and a 2012 repost. A reader who counts Taubes (2006) as settling the bullet would say the bullet is settled in dimension 3 (the level sets of Hamiltonians on symplectic 4-manifolds); the bullet quantifies over all dimensions, so that is a partial answer. A reader who counts Viterbo (1987) and the restricted classes would say the bullet is open but with many special cases settled.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A journal acceptance, an expert verification or a published refutation of Oh's argument, or a repaired arXiv version whose Case 2 shows the extracted orbit is nonconstant. (b) The reason for Ma's 2011 withdrawal and the content of v5 (2012). (c) The proof text of Oh's v1 Section 7.3.2 and its bubbling analysis, read in full. (d) A 2025-2026 journal survey or Quanta-type report on the Weinstein conjecture, which would show whether the community regards any of the 2024-2026 claims as settled. (e) Reading the openai/math index with the summarising fetch replaced by a verbatim read of the abstracts of families 062, 087, 143, 340-347, to confirm none concerns closed orbits on contact-type levels.

judgement.why: The only post-snapshot event aimed at the statement itself is Oh's December 2024 preprint. On its face it is whole (closed Reeb orbits on every compact contact manifold), but the author withdrew it and named the exact gap in the key step: the orbit produced may be constant. That makes it knocked_down. Ma's 2000 general claim is not_credible because several signals line up: no uptake in 26 years, surveys after it still call the problem open, an unexplained withdrawal followed by a repost, and an overlap flag. The pre-snapshot class results (Viterbo in R^{2n}, Taubes in dimension 3, Albers-Hofer, Geiges-Zehmisch and others) are each a case, because the statement quantifies over every symplectic manifold and every dimension. Journal publication counts as digestion where the record shows it; Hofer-Viterbo, Hofer 1993, ACH 2004 and GZ 2014 have no recorded check, so they stay unreviewed. Every other post-snapshot paper answers a different question: multiplicity counts on classes where existence is already known, almost existence, 3D orbit structure, chord conjectures, or which magnetic levels are of contact type. Those are variants. The singular b-contact counterexample concerns a changed question, so it is a variant and its object does not bear on the statement.
judgement.doubts: Hofer-Viterbo and Hofer 1993 are dated and scoped from Wikipedia and secondary summaries only. Viterbo's first public argument may be 1986, but it falls before the snapshot either way. Oh's acknowledgements were not seen, so the AI 'none' for that event rests on the parts that were read.
